slots.hypothesis: Lottery preference (skewness premium). In retail-heavy A-shares, investors overpay for stocks whose returns come from a few upward jumps: right-skewed minute returns, with upside semivariance taking a large share of realized variance. These stocks then underperform. The signals measure the shape of the intraday return distribution with scale-free third-moment or sign-asymmetry statistics: day_skew(Ret), RSJ = day_signed_ratio(Ret, mul(Ret, Ret)), skew of the VWAP path and of 5-minute log changes, kurtosis, the es_ratio hi-lo tail difference, minute MAX/(MAX-MIN), close location in the day's range, the 20-day daily skew, the daily up-minus-down semideviation, the 5-day minus 60-day skew shift, and skew demeaned within price deciles (a tick-size proxy check). Each is made persistent with cross_mean(.,20). The five controls only cover first moments (reversal), second moments and levels (volatility, amount level and dispersion) and size, so the third moment is uncontrolled. The effect should persist out of sample because it is a behavioral preference that short-sale limits stop arbitrageurs from correcting, and the trait is slow-moving. 12 seeds.

How volume lines up with price reveals who is trading. Positive-feedback chasing (volume follows price, or concentrates at high prices and in up-minutes) leaves temporary overpricing that unwinds. Liquidity-providing volume (concentrated at lows and in down-minutes) is underpriced. This follows Llorente et al. 2002 and De Long et al. 1990. The seeds are: intraday day_corr(Close, Volume) and day_corr(Ret, Volume); lead-lag correlations in both directions using in_delay; volume acceleration against return; |Ret| against volume; tick-rule (day_signed_ratio(Ret, Amt)) and BVC (day_wmean(sigmoid(in_zscore_expand(Ret)), Amt)) order-imbalance proxies; skew of the signed dollar flow; 20-day interday price-volume and return-amount cross_corr; the 20-day stddev and the 5-day minus 60-day shift of intraday correlation; and a cs_flip_by_state version keyed to the market's trading-volume state. All are correlations, bounded ratios or skews, so the units of amount and volatility cancel. They read the alignment and ordering of volume and price, which none of the controls contain. 14 seeds.
